2.2 **A single linkage block has no split central idempotent.** $\mathcal O_\alpha$ is a single linkage block by [[lem-type-a-tableau-central-summands-are-single-linkage-blocks]]: it admits no decomposition into two nonzero orthogonal factors. A central idempotent $f=f^2\ne0$ of $A$ with $f\ne1$ would split the projective generator $Q=Qf\oplus Q(1-f)$ into two nonzero summands whose Hom-spaces in both directions vanish, because every morphism between them is annihilated by composing with $f$ on either side in the two possible orders; this exhibits $\mathcal O_\alpha$ as the product of the two nonzero full subcategories generated by these summands, contradicting single-linkage. Let $(G,T)$ be a split reductive group over $k$ with root datum $(X,\Phi,\alpha\mapsto\alpha^\vee)$ ([[def-roots-and-root-groups-of-a-split-reductive-group]]). Then: (a) $W(G,T)=N_G(T)/T$ is a finite constant group scheme and $W(G,T)(k')=N_G(T)(k')/T(k')$ for every field $k'\supseteq k$; (b) every split maximal torus of $G$ lies in a Borel subgroup, and every Borel subgroup of $G$ containing $T$ is of the form $P_G(\lambda)$ for a regular cocharacter $\lambda$, hence is split; (c) $W(G,T)$ acts simply transitively on the finite set of Borel subgroups of $G$ containing $T$, and the map sending a Borel subgroup to its system of positive roots is a bijection onto the set of positive systems; (d) there is a canonical isomorphism $W(G,T)\cong W(R)$ of finite groups, and $W(G,T)$ is generated by the simple reflections $s_\alpha$, $\alpha\in\Delta$, for any base $\Delta$; (e) for a Borel subgroup $B\supseteq T$, for $w\in W(G,T)$ and a representative $n_w\in N_G(T)(k)$, the double coset $Bn_wB$ depends only on $w$ and $n_wU_\alpha n_w^{-1}=U_{w\alpha}$ for all roots $\alpha$.
